prompt: A computer's folders contain files and other folders, all inside one top folder.
why: Every folder sits inside exactly one parent, all the way up to one top folder. One root with nested children is a tree.
trap: There are no loops, so a general graph is more than you need.

prompt: In a company org chart, everyone has one manager except the CEO.
why: Everyone has exactly one manager, and only the CEO has none. One parent each and a single root make a tree.
trap: One manager each means no extra links.

prompt: A web page's HTML has tags nested inside tags.
why: Each tag sits inside exactly one parent tag, up to the html tag at the top. The browser stores this nesting as a tree called the DOM.
trap: A parser may use a stack, but the structure is a tree.

prompt: A family tree is traced down from one ancestor through children and grandchildren.
why: Traced down from one ancestor, each child branches from one parent line. A single root branching downward is a tree.
trap: Each child has many descendants, not one next item.

prompt: A book's table of contents has chapters, each with sections, each with subsections.
tells: each with sections, each with subsections
why: Chapters hold sections, which hold subsections, each inside exactly one parent. Nested levels under one top are a tree.
trap: It's more than a flat list.

prompt: A menu has categories that open into subcategories, ending in items.
why: Categories open into subcategories and end in items, with each item under one category. Branches ending in leaves are a tree.
trap: There's one path to each item.
